Why are black olives so much weaker than men?

Black olives aren’t “weaker than men”—they’re food, not people. “Black” describes the olive’s ripeness or curing process, not a group with traits comparable to humans.

If you meant nutritional strength: olives contain mostly fat and relatively little protein, so they’re not comparable to a person’s physical strength.
